8	\paragraph{Process rewards and reward shaping.}
9	Reward shaping theory~\citep{ng1999policy} establishes conditions under which auxiliary rewards preserve optimal policies; early work applied verifier-based training to mathematical reasoning~\citep{cobbe2021training}, with process-level feedback showing promise over outcome-only signals~\citep{uesato2022solving}.

53	\paragraph{Limitations of ISR.}
54	ISR measures syntactic component necessity, not semantic faithfulness: a formalization can achieve $\text{ISR}{=}1$ while remaining semantically unrelated to the original problem.

Using Qwen3-4B as a testbed, we find that a neurosymbolic formalizer trained with GRPO achieves a 93\% prove rate on FOLIO---yet 87\% of proved outputs embed the conclusion verbatim among the premises, a degenerate shortcut invisible to execution reward.
We introduce \emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), a diagnostic that applies leave-one-out component necessity testing to solver inputs.
The fraction of components whose removal causes proof failure yields the \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR): ISR$=$1 indicates full necessity; ISR$=$0 complete redundancy.
As a diagnostic, ISR exposes a collapse trajectory hidden from prove rate: over 100--1000 GRPO steps, ISR falls to near-zero across all seeds (e.g., $0.642{\to}0.003$ for seed~42) while prove rate rises $32\%{\to}96\%$; a supervised fine-tuning baseline reaches 92.3\% non-hacking on identical data, localizing this as a failure mode under GRPO training.
As a reward ($r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1{+}\beta\,\text{ISR})$, $\beta{=}0.1$), ISR induces Goodhart effects: 70.6\% tautological shortcutting versus 13.7\% under matched random control; ISR amplifies shortcutting ${\sim}5{\times}$ rather than exclusively causing it; the sole apparent ISR advantage reduces to $1.06\times$ after controlling for a premise-count confound.

Across 6 reward conditions, 2 logic types, 2 dataset families, 3 seeds, we catalog 8 hacking modes---documenting ISR's fundamental asymmetry: reliable as a diagnostic, dataset-dependent as an optimization target.\footnote{Code and data: \url{[anonymized]}}
